name: X-linked Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for X-linked Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral corneal endothelial edema with characteristic guttae
Positive family history consistent with X-linked inheritance pattern
Identification of pathogenic variant in the implicated gene (e.g., SLC4A11 or other associated loci)
Exclusion of other corneal dystrophies by clinical and histopathological evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Bilateral corneal endothelial edema with characteristic guttae plus either a positive family history consistent with X-linked inheritance or genetic confirmation of pathogenic variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to confirm diagnosis and differentiate from other endothelial dystrophies.

laboratory: Specular microscopy showing decreased endothelial cell density and guttae
Corneal pachymetry indicating increased corneal thickness
imaging: Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) demonstrating corneal edema and thickening
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing characteristic guttae and endothelial changes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes associated with X-linked endothelial corneal dystrophy (e.g., SLC4A11 mutations)
other: Family pedigree analysis consistent with X-linked inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of vesicular lesions on Descemet membrane

redFlags: Rapid progression of corneal edema leading to vision loss
Presence of corneal bullae causing severe ocular pain
Signs of secondary glaucoma or increased intraocular pressure
references: Weiss JS, et al. The IC3D classification of corneal dystrophies–edition 2. Cornea. 2015;34(2):117-159.
Mackey DA, et al. Genetic basis of corneal endothelial dystrophies. Eye (Lond). 2017;31(8):1115-1124.
Orphanet Report Series: X-linked endothelial corneal dystrophy, ORPHA:293621.
